subject: Private GPU pool sizing assumptions & cross-team checklist (Aster Analytics)

Subject: Private GPU pool sizing assumptions & cross-team checklist (Aster Analytics)

Hi Jim —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Attached is the initial capacity workbook that maps the throughput targets you described to a proposed private GPU pool topology and the operational checklist we'll need for cutover. High-level assumptions in the spreadsheet:

- Target steady-state throughput: 75K tokens/sec sustained (equivalent to ~200 concurrent inference streams at your baseline prompt length).
- Peak burst budget: 220K tokens/sec for short windows (5–10 minutes) driven by daily batch jobs.
- Headroom target: 30% above steady-state for safe autoscale handoffs.
- Warm-cache strategy: prefix/KV warmup during scheduled warm windows; estimated 8–12 minutes to reach steady tail latency for large-model runs.
- Network profile: dual 100Gbps spine with 25% oversubscription at rack NIC level; we recommend RDMA-friendly NICs for KV/cache traffic if you plan >100ms sequence lengths.

Questions we need answers to from your side before we finalize sizing:
1) Expected 90th/99th percentile prompt length distribution for production traffic (tokens).
2) Whether your on-prem environment supports SR-IOV or other NIC passthrough for low-latency networking.
3) Maintenance windows and any blackout periods for autoscaler-driven node reclamation.

Next steps: if the assumptions look reasonable, we'll schedule a cross-team design review where Karthik (infra) will propose the rack/pod topology and Laura will outline the SLA templates and escalation playbooks. Ben will follow up on procurement timelines for reserved capacity pricing.

Attachments: aster_capacity_workbook.xlsx (xlsx, 145 KB), vpc_network_topology_v2.png (png, 420 KB)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0184

- We can confirm steady-state intent of ~75K tokens/sec; however, our nightly analytics batch at 02:00 local can spike to ~180K tokens/sec for 8–12 minutes. The burst cadence is predictable.
- Our infra team confirms SR-IOV support on the planned deployment hardware (Dell R760 with Mellanox CX6).
- Maintenance windows: weekly patching Sundays 03:00–05:00; we would prefer no destructive autoscaler operations during that window.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide a recommended slab-sizing that minimizes partial-GPU packing for our workload? We'd prefer a configuration that reduces cold-starts during the 02:00 batch.
2) Can we limit cross-rack failover by default to avoid saturating east–west fabric?

I'll loop in procurement in case there are questions about reserved-node terms.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Private GPU pool sizing assumptions & cross-team checklist (Aster Analytics)

Folks —

Quick technical readout after reviewing Aster's updated numbers and SR-IOV confirmation. High-level recommendations:

1) Slab recommendation: choose the large-slab (4-GPU logical slab) for the primary pool used by nightly batch. Rationale: the batch workload is long-running and benefits from contiguous GPU allocation (lower KV cache misses, reduced inter-GPU handshake cost). Large-slab reduces cold-start frequency by ~60% in our simulations.

2) Secondary steady-state pool: small-slab (1–2 GPU) for inference serving during business hours. This gives better packing for spiky API traffic and reduces unit-cost for low-concurrency flows.

3) Autoscaler & failover policy: implement an intra-rack fill-first policy with a spill threshold at 85% rack utilization. Only when all racks exceed 85% utilization should we spill cross-rack. This keeps east–west egress bounded. We'll expose the spill threshold as a runtime knob in the console.

4) Network: with dual 100Gbps spine and Mellanox CX6 NICs, configure a dedicated VLAN for KV/cache traffic and enable flow-control (PFC) for the priority lane. RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCEv2) recommended for large-sequence KV pulls.

5) Warmup: run a rolling warm window starting T-30 minutes before the 02:00 batch and ensure the warm-pool has a minimum alive time of 90 minutes to amortize warm cost.

6) Monitoring & SLOs: 99th pct latency target of 280ms token tail under steady-state; 99.9th pct resilience target for batch completion under burst is 95% success. We will provide a telemetry dashboard with token-level traces and a warm-pool health signal.

I'll attach a short simulation summary in the drive link; the simulation uses Aster's token-length histogram to project cold-start probability across slab choices.

Karthik Iyer
